paragraphs.heading: Free, or forced
paragraphs.edited: So notice, when we say God is all-powerful, we don't mean God can do anything we can just conceive of. We mean God can do everything that power can do that is consistent with his moral nature. But here's the key that this challenge misses. Even God can't make a world with beings who are genuinely free and then force us to always do what is good, because if God forces us to always do what is good, we're not free. And if we're truly free, then God is not forcing us to always do what is good. So yes, God is all-powerful. Yes, God can and will stop evil. But logically speaking, God can no more make a world with genuine free will, where humans make meaningful choices, and then turn around and force us to always choose what is good.

paragraphs.heading: God's megaphone
paragraphs.edited: C.S. Lewis once said, "God whispers in our pleasure, but he shouts in our pain. Pain is God's megaphone to arouse a deaf world." What was he saying? He's saying that in our pleasure and in the joys of life, sometimes we think about God, but maybe, because God is good and because he's so powerful, he can even use our pain and our suffering and the evil in the world, turn it toward good, and draw us to rely upon him and trust.
